patterns.rhetorical_purpose: Signal that the compared systems are well-regarded/current.
move_sequence: Describe the 10 evaluated systems as 'state-of-the-art' without naming the specific comparison set or a date scope in the same sentence.
patterns.reader_question_answered: N/A -- this is the anti-pattern entry (signature/repair), not a move to imitate.
patterns.signature: 'we ... evaluate 10 state-of-theart retrieval systems' (Abstract) -- matches anti_patterns.md B3 (unbacked SOTA: 'state-of-the-art' without a named benchmark, full comparison set, and date).
patterns.reader_effect: A careful reader cannot tell from the phrase alone what 'state-of-the-art' is being claimed relative to, or as of when.
patterns.repair_principle: Either qualify fully (name the comparison set and time scope) or drop the label and let the systems' own citations and the results table carry the credibility.
patterns.quote: we ... evaluate 10 state-of-theart retrieval systems including lexical, sparse, dense, late-interaction and re-ranking architectures

scope_note: Per run-specific constraints (no web search), this anti-pattern was identified only from project/paper.txt itself rather than from a broader verified corpus of prior papers. It is logged here as a caution for the overclaim audit (workflow step 17): the adapted draft must not repeat an unqualified 'state-of-the-art' claim in its own Abstract/Introduction (see anti_patterns.md B3, lint rule B3-sota).
